Hours before it was set to be signed, the White House scrapped its AI safety executive order.

According to Axios, Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk, and David Sacks called the president directly before the decision. A White House source said the president "just hates regulation."

Regardless of where you stand politically, the business implications are concrete. The US now has no federal AI safety framework on the horizon. That does not simplify things for companies — it complicates them.

Here is why: the regulatory vacuum will be filled unevenly. State-level rules, EU AI Act requirements, and industry self-governance will create a patchwork that is harder to navigate than a single federal standard would have been.

For business leaders, three things become true immediately. First, your internal AI governance framework is now your public standard — customers and investors will hold you to it. Second, the gap between US and EU regulation just widened, adding complexity for any company operating internationally. Third, speed of AI deployment increases, but so does reputational exposure.

The organizations that build rigorous AI governance voluntarily will earn trust that becomes a lasting competitive advantage.
